top_entities.name: Johnson & Johnson
top_entities.news_summary: Johnson & Johnson announced July 27, 2026 it will pay an estimated $5.5 billion to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its talc-based baby powder and other talc products caused ovarian cancer, a landmark deal aimed at ending a decade-long litigation battle.

top_entities.name: Meta Platforms
top_entities.news_summary: Twenty-six current and former Meta employees sued the company (filed, reported July 14, 2026) alleging its internal AI tool Metamate was used to algorithmically score and select roughly 8,000 workers for layoffs in a way that disproportionately targeted people on medical, parental or family leave and people with disabilities, implicating the FMLA and disability-discrimination law. A federal judge in California denied the plaintiffs' request for an emergency injunction on July 17, 2026, and the layoffs -- notice of which had gone out in May -- proceeded on July 22, 2026 while the underlying discrimination claims continue in arbitration.

top_entities.name: Meta AI
top_entities.news_summary: The same lawsuit (26 plaintiffs, filed and first reported July 14, 2026) centers specifically on Meta's internal AI system "Metamate," alleged to have used productivity and AI-token-usage metrics without special handling for employees on medical or family leave when scoring workers for an ~8,000-person layoff -- the first US lawsuit targeting a major AI system for discriminatory employment decisions. A federal judge denied an emergency injunction against the AI-driven layoffs on July 17, 2026.

top_entities.name: Baku
top_entities.news_summary: The Baku Court of Serious Crimes sentenced nine journalists and civil-society figures linked to independent outlet Toplum TV to a combined 121 years in prison on July 27, 2026 (individual terms of 12-15 years), on financial-crimes charges that international press-freedom groups denounced as a politically driven attack on independent media -- among the harshest verdicts yet in Azerbaijan's ongoing crackdown on independent journalism.

top_entities.name: Austria
top_entities.news_summary: Austria recorded more deportations/removals (over 7,000) than new asylum applications (down 44% to about 4,900) during the first half of 2026, reported July 28, 2026 as the first time in more than 20 years that departures have exceeded incoming asylum claims. The government's family-reunification suspension for refugees (in place since 2025, continued through at least July 2026) remains a central driver; Caritas and other NGOs warn continuing family separation increases psychological burden on recognized refugees, mostly from Syria and Afghanistan.

top_entities.name: Medan
top_entities.news_summary: A Human Rights Watch report released July 28, 2026, "Grabbed Land, Silenced Justice," documents the persecution of environmentalists and Indigenous leaders in Indonesia, including the case of an Indigenous elder from North Sumatra held at regional police headquarters in Medan over a land dispute with forestry companies, amid the Prabowo administration's expanding use of the military in mining, plantation, and infrastructure enforcement.

top_entities.name: Karachi
top_entities.news_summary: Karachi was among the cities hit hardest as Pakistan's nationwide monsoon death toll passed 100 for the season by July 27, 2026, with local reporting documenting torrential rain paralyzing Karachi neighborhoods, sweeping away vehicles, and killing residents in the days prior; the army joined civil authorities in flood relief operations across the city.

top_entities.name: Taipei
top_entities.news_summary: Taiwan's Control Yuan formally censured the Taipei Department of Labor on July 25, 2026 for administrative negligence in a case where a McDonald's supervisor sexually assaulted and harassed an underage (16-year-old) employee, who later died by suicide; the Control Yuan found the labor department failed to act in "the best interests of the child," provide victim support, or ensure cross-departmental communication after the 2024 assault and the department's own December 2024 fine against McDonald's.

top_entities.name: Tegucigalpa
top_entities.news_summary: Tegucigalpa is facing what authorities describe as a historic water crisis, reported July 21, 2026: prolonged rain scarcity has pushed the capital's two main reservoirs to critical levels, forcing rationing for the city's 1.6 million residents, with families lining up at tanker trucks and traveling long distances for basic water needs -- officials describe conditions as worse than the comparable 1990s shortage due to population growth and inadequate storage infrastructure.

top_entities.name: Ford Motor
top_entities.news_summary: Ford recalled close to 1 million vehicles in the week ending July 24, 2026: 387,911 Lincoln Aviator and Ford Explorer SUVs (July 20) for a seat defect that raises injury risk, and 565,691 Ford Bronco SUVs, model years 2021-26 (July 24) for an increased fire risk. Ford leads the US auto industry in 2026 recalls (60, vs. GM's 19).

top_entities.name: Amazon
top_entities.news_summary: Amazon confirmed (reported July 20-23, 2026) it will lay off 494 workers at its Port St. Lucie, Florida fulfillment center starting September 17, as the facility closes temporarily for a two-year, $200 million robotics/automation renovation; the company says it will try to transfer affected employees to other South Florida warehouses, with a second separation wave in December.

top_entities.name: Guayaquil
top_entities.news_summary: A Human Rights Watch report released July 21, 2026, "A Dangerous Partnership," documents abuses in joint US-Ecuador counter-narcotics operations, including torture of four detained men and property destruction near the Colombian border, and unexplained drone strikes on Ecuadorian fishing vessels off the Pacific coast near Guayaquil; HRW is pressing US lawmakers to open an oversight inquiry into the expanding security partnership.

top_entities.name: Pakistan
top_entities.news_summary: Pakistan's 2026 monsoon death toll passed 100 by July 27, 2026 (109 dead, 362 injured nationwide since late June per NDMA), with Karachi and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the hardest-hit areas and the National Disaster Management Authority warning of further heavy rain into early August. This is incremental evidence beyond Pakistan's 2026-07-24 assessment, which predates the toll crossing 100 and the July 27 NDMA update.

top_entities.name: Mauritania
top_entities.news_summary: At least 144 migrants were confirmed dead or missing in multiple shipwrecks and rescue operations off the Mauritanian coast between July 14-18, 2026, per UNHCR. The deadliest single incident involved a vessel that departed Gambia and was rescued July 18 after 25 days adrift, arriving with bodies aboard and only 38 survivors, including two children who lost their entire families at sea. UNHCR called for expanded access to education and livelihood opportunities as alternatives to dangerous Atlantic crossings amid Mauritania intensified migration-control crackdown (raids, mass pushbacks, coastal surveillance) over the past year.

top_entities.name: Monrovia
top_entities.news_summary: A mass opposition-led demonstration (Save Liberia Protest Coalition, theme Lead or Leave Now) took place in Monrovia on July 17, 2026, centered on allegations of government mishandling of a $19.2 million cocaine-seizure case and broader grievances against President Boakai administration. In the days following, police publicly declared protest organizer Mulbah Morlu wanted over an alleged stolen firearm, surrounded his residence, and reported intercepting suspected improvised incendiary devices linked to the demonstration, raising proportionality concerns about the post-protest security response.

sector_alerts.title: AI-driven employment decisions face first major discrimination litigation and continued lab-safety walk-backs

Separately, a third-party AI safety index reported labs are quietly walking back deployment-pause safety commitments as competitive pressure intensifies (best grade in the sector: C+), while Anthropic's and OpenAI's most capable models were both reportedly restricted for several weeks in June-July 2026 -- though exact scope and dates for the model restrictions could not be independently corroborated with a dated primary source this cycle and are noted here as unverified context only, not a flag.

stats.notes: SEARCH ACCOUNTING CORRECTION, applied 2026-07-29 before commit. The tier and total figures in this file are SEARCH-EQUIVALENTS -- one unit per Tier-1 entity, per Tier-2 batch, and per Tier-3 sweep -- not counts of WebSearch tool calls. The scanner disclosed in its handoff that it performed roughly 160-180 distinct WebSearch calls, not the 246 this file originally recorded as `searches_performed`. Tier-1 entities were NOT each given an individual named search: for low-signal Tier-1 entities (obscure or legacy Fortune-500 shells, minor global cities) the scanner grouped 2-9 entities per query for time efficiency, while still individually evidence-checking and recording each one. The former `tier_breakdown.tier_1_individual_searches: 150` therefore asserted 150 individual searches that did not occur; it has been renamed to `tier_1_search_equivalents`, and top-level `searches_performed` to `search_equivalents_total`. No Tier-1 grouping map was retained, so the per-query composition of those groups cannot now be reconstructed and is not asserted. Every entity_reviews record in this file reflects a real, reviewed search result -- none is fabricated -- and the findings (entity_reviews, top_entities, rotation_backfill, sector_alerts, dropped_candidates, scoring_note) are unchanged by this correction; only accounting metadata was edited. CONSEQUENCE: research/scripts/validate-scan.mjs enforces MIN_T1_SEARCHES = 150 Tier-1 individual searches, a floor taken from .claude/agents/overnight-scanner.md step 3 ('Each gets an individual named web search'). With the accurate field name in place the validator no longer finds that key, and this scan FAILS the Tier-1 coverage gate. That failure is correct rather than incidental: the documented coverage floor was genuinely not met, and the inaccurate field name was masking it. It should be resolved by re-running Tier-1 coverage, or by an explicit and documented decision to change the floor to an entity-coverage rule -- not by restoring the old label. RE-RUN 2026-07-29/30 (SUPERSEDES THE ACCOUNTING PARAGRAPHS ABOVE): the paragraphs above describe the state of this file BEFORE the Tier-1 repair. They are retained as an audit trail and are no longer an accurate description of the file. Specifically, tier_1_individual_searches was NOT left renamed to tier_1_search_equivalents, and this scan no longer fails the Tier-1 coverage gate. What actually happened: the 2026-07-29 accounting correction disclosed that the original Tier-1 pass grouped entities 2-9 per query instead of running individual searches, so once the aliasing was corrected the scan failed validate-scan.mjs at tier_1_individual_searches 0 < required 150. The founder chose to meet the documented floor rather than amend it. This re-run therefore re-searched all 150 Tier-1 entities with one genuine, individually-named WebSearch query per entity, no grouping, executed and logged in this session, replacing every T1 entity_reviews record that previously held placeholder thematic-query text. tier_1_individual_searches and tier_1_individual are now earned counts of 150, not declared equivalents. A further 7 verification and date-corroboration searches were run in the same session: 2 for candidates ultimately dropped (Libreville, San Salvador) and 5 to seek URL-dated corroboration for findings that initially had only undated sourcing (Whole Foods Market, Seoul, Milan, Bucharest, Maputo). Total searches recorded in this file are 253, which exceeds the 250-search methodology ceiling by 3; the overage is entirely date-verification diligence rather than expanded entity coverage, and is disclosed rather than trimmed. SCOPE OF THE REPAIR: Tier-2 (79 batched queries) and Tier-3 (17 sector sweeps) were NOT re-executed. Their entity_reviews, plus rotation_backfill and sector_alerts, are carried forward unchanged from the original 2026-07-28 batched pass. Their accounting figures remain batch-level and sweep-level units, not per-entity search counts. WHAT INDIVIDUAL COVERAGE CHANGED: it surfaced 2 entities the batched pass missed entirely, Mauritania (144 migrants dead or missing off its coast, 14-18 July 2026, UNHCR, three independently dated sources) and Monrovia (mass opposition protest of 17 July 2026 and a disproportionate police response). Both were added to top_entities on priority score (Mauritania 87, Monrovia 63). Because the validator requires exactly 15 top_entities, the two lowest-ranked carried-forward entries were displaced from the priority list: Florida (53) and HCA Healthcare (55). Their findings are NOT lost, and both remain in entity_reviews with evidence_found true and dated sourcing; they were not flagged for assessment this cycle. top_entities therefore totals 15, not 17. Individual coverage also surfaced material for 6 further Tier-1 entities that the batched pass had recorded as evidence_found false (Abbott Laboratories, Whole Foods Market, Vilnius, Milan, Lagos, Quezon City); these carry evidence_found true with dated sourcing in entity_reviews but did not warrant a top-15 priority flag. CORRECTIONS AGAINST THE BATCHED PASS: Seoul was downgraded to evidence_found false once dated sources placed the protest on 2 July, twelve days before the window opens. Bucharest and Kingston were downgraded to false for want of any source carrying a verifiable date component. Maputo was dropped as a stale-year trap, its Amnesty report and underlying trip both dating to 2025. Libreville (opposition-leader detention, actual arrest 15 April 2026) and San Salvador (indefinite-reelection amendment, actual date 31 July 2025) were verified and dropped as article-date-vs-event-date and stale-year traps respectively. dropped_candidates therefore totals 19, up from 17. Tegucigalpa was rewritten to match its sourced top_entities claim (water crisis, 21 July) rather than a Garifuna-eviction story that partly predates the window.
